Turns on Internal Work Orders. Switching the toggle on opens the modal of frame 1b.

After the modal the toggle is on and saved. The tab stays light: two hint lines, one of them a link to the Internal Work Orders page where the categories live (frame 2a). Later turn-ons use Save settings like every other toggle and open no modal.

A page of its own under Administration > Service, like Labor Rates and Canned Lines. Two tabs. The starting set is seeded when the setting is first turned on: General Internal (the default) here, Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback on the other tab. The QuickBooks column shows the expense account for the location you are in, as the parts Categories page shows Products and Services; Not set means ShopView Review until one is picked. The shop adds its own (Company Vehicle Maintenance, Shop Equipment Maintenance) or archives what it does not use. The same accounts are also editable in Integrations > QuickBooks > ShopView Accounts, one row per category, for shops used to mapping there (frame 9).

rows.text: Same page, second tab. The third column says whether the category requires the original work order (Warranty and Comeback do). Several categories can share an account.

New No Charge Category, or a click on a row (Edit). Name, the QuickBooks expense account per connected location (one small table, so a multi-location shop sets everything here) and whether the category requires the original work order. Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the account is picked from the chart that is already there. Archive is in the row menu; a category is never deleted, so old work orders and reports keep it.

Same dialog for an internal category: name, the QuickBooks expense account and Default category. The default is used by every internal customer without a category of its own and cannot be archived. A small shop keeps General Internal and never opens this.

While the setting is off the menu item is disabled with the tooltip "Turn on Internal Work Orders in Settings > Work Orders." and the page is read-only with the same note; nothing is deleted. Same rule as the Internal customer checkbox (frame 6).

rows.text: Informational only; nothing is required or blocked.

The checkbox is the only place the flag is set. Save flags the customer; when it already has open billable work orders the dialog of frame 7 follows. Shown only while the setting is on. Not shown on New Customer.

Opens when the checkbox is unticked, before the dialog is saved. Open internal work orders are not touched.

Same mapping, second door: one row per category under Cost of Parts, grouped Internal work orders and No Charge work orders. Editing here or on the category writes the same value for this location; a new category adds its row here by itself. Cost of Parts and Inventory Asset are used as today for the credit side.
Same page when a category has no account at this location: its row is empty with the warning. Set it here or on the category, same thing.

On a flagged customer Min is accepted without a percentage; it is the shop supplies default on internal work orders. Default internal category shows only while the customer is flagged; a shop with several internal customers (Fleet, Shop Equipment, Facility) gives each its own.

Asset of an internal customer: its own internal category. The QuickBooks mark sits in the explanation: categories are mapped to QuickBooks expense accounts. Priority: asset, then customer, then General Internal.
Turning the setting off hides the hint lines and the customer badges and leaves the flags on the customers.
